chapter: Eddie Heywood, the organ and later work
title: Late-career travel and albums
summary: He toured Europe with the Harlem Blues and Jazz Band after Milt Buckner and T-Bone Walker, made RCA and Master Jazz albums, and recorded at Frank's Steak House.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: I think what we'll finish up with is your last five years, to see what you've been doing recently.
I've been going abroad with the Harlem Blues and Jazz Band. I went over twice to Europe. That's after I went with Milt Buckner and T-Bone Walker.
And you've also not mentioned the fact that you made an album... You made two albums for RCA, didn't you?
Oh yeah. That was in about '67.
Yes. Then you made another one for Master Jazz.
Oh yeah, those. Boy, I wish I could buy them back.
No! And did you make one in Europe?
I made several things in Europe. I don't know if they put them out or not. But the record I made with Dennis Preston...
There was one later made at Frank's Steak House.
Timme Rosencrantz put out one of something that I made at Frank's Steak House. I don't remember what...
You made with him? I didn't know that.
Yeah. They were floating all around Scandinavia for quite a while. It's Ronnie Cole and myself, and there's a saxophonist (what's his name?), Bob Lema. He's from Brooklyn.
He's good. He's talented. We made a little noise at Frank's Steak House...
